mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 7.0% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that may prompt central bank intervention, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has exceeded 7.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a contraction in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness; this combination predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both RSAFS and HOUST decline for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with CPIAUCSL annual rate > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 0.5% for three consecutive months, it indicates an ultra-loose monetary policy that fuels risk appetite and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has been below 0.5% for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 6 months signals robust economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO has increased for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) falls below 50,000 for two consecutive months, it indicates a slowing labor market that may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS monthly change has been below 50,000 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) for three consecutive months, manufacturing activity weakens, leading to lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO has been below 100 for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
